# Original comic fixtures

All PNG artwork and ComicInfo metadata are generated by
`python3 tests/generate_comic_fixtures.py` using Python's standard library.
JPEG/WebP assets were encoded from original flat-color test images; the third
WebP has zero alpha to test compositing. No published comics are included.

RAR fixtures were generated from `rar-source/pages/` and `ComicInfo.xml` with
RAR 6.24 for Linux x64 (test preparation only, not a distributed dependency):

```sh
cd tests/fixtures/comics/rar-source
rar a -idq -cfg- -m3 -md4m -ma4 -s- -ep1 ../sample-rar4.cbr pages ComicInfo.xml
rar a -idq -cfg- -m3 -md4m -ma4 -s -ep1 ../sample-rar4-solid.cbr pages ComicInfo.xml
rar a -idq -cfg- -m3 -md4m -ma5 -s- -ep1 ../sample-rar5.cbr pages ComicInfo.xml
rar a -idq -cfg- -m3 -md4m -ma5 -s -ep1 ../sample-rar5-solid.cbr pages ComicInfo.xml
rar a -idq -cfg- -m3 -md4m -ma4 -ptest-password -ep1 ../password.cbr pages ComicInfo.xml
cp ../sample-rar4.cbr ../rar-renamed.cbz
```

The compressed RAR binaries are checked in so CI needs no RAR creation tool.
RAR tool source: https://www.rarlab.com/rar/rarlinux-x64-624.tar.gz.
The application decodes RAR using libarchive and LGPLv3 unarr, not this tool.

Additional rejection fixtures use `zip -P test-password password.cbz
pages/Page1.PNG` and `rar a -m0 -ma4` / `-ma5 -v1k -ep1 split.rar pages
ComicInfo.xml`; only each first volume is kept as `split-rar4.cbr` or
`split-rar5.cbr`.
